learn.hook: Honey, bamboo, fruits and fresh air: a forest is like a giant free gift shop!
points: A forest is a large area thickly covered with trees, bushes and other plants. Many animals live there.
Forests give us wood, bamboo, fruits, honey, gum and medicinal plants.
Many communities live in and near forests. They collect forest things carefully and take only what they need.
Leaves of the sal tree are stitched into plates and bowls called pattal and dona.
Tree roots hold the soil in place, and forests help keep the air clean and cool.

example.q: Think it through: A hillside loses all its trees. When heavy rain comes, what happens to the soil?
steps: Tree roots hold the soil together like a net.
Without trees, nothing holds the soil.
Rain water washes the loose soil away.
example.answer: The soil gets washed away, because there are no roots to hold it.

learn.reallife: Look around your home. Which things came from a forest? Maybe your wooden chair, a bamboo basket or a jar of honey!

games.title: From the forest or not?
items: Honey
Bamboo
Sal leaf plates
Gum
Sea salt
Plastic bottle

games.title: Forest facts
items: Tree roots help hold the soil in place.
Roots grip the soil so rain does not wash it away.
Forests are home to many animals and birds.
Forests give animals food and shelter.
Taking only what we need from a forest helps it last longer.
When we take a little, the forest has time to grow back.
Cutting down all the trees has no effect on animals.
Animals lose their homes and food when trees are cut.
Sal leaves can be made into plates.
Sal leaf plates called pattal are used at many feasts.

quiz.q: Which of these do we get from forests?
quiz.explain: Bees make honey in forests, and honey collectors gather it.
quiz.mistake: Does not know which things come from forests

quiz.q: How do tree roots help the soil?
options: They make the soil fly away
They hold the soil in place
quiz.explain: Roots spread through the soil like a net and stop rain from washing it away.
quiz.mistake: Does not link roots with holding soil

quiz.q: Plates made by stitching sal leaves together are called…
quiz.explain: Pattal are plates made from leaves like sal. They are used at many meals and feasts.
quiz.mistake: Confuses leaf plates with metal or clay utensils

quiz.q: What happens to animals when a forest is cut down?
options: They lose their homes and food
quiz.explain: Forests give animals food and shelter. Without trees, they have nowhere to live.
quiz.mistake: Thinks cutting trees does not affect animals

quiz.q: Why do forest communities take only what they need from the forest?
options: So that the forest can keep growing and giving
Because they do not like fruits
Because the forest is far away
quiz.explain: If we take only a little, plants and trees can grow back, and the forest lasts for a long time.
quiz.mistake: Does not understand careful use of nature

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a forest product?
quiz.explain: Steel is made from iron in factories. Bamboo, gum and herbs come from forests.
quiz.mistake: Thinks everything we use comes from forests

quiz.q: Which of these is a way forests help us?
options: They make the land very hot
They give clean air and shade
quiz.explain: Trees give out oxygen and give shade. Forests keep the air cleaner and cooler.
quiz.mistake: Does not know how forests help the air and climate

quiz.q: Bamboo from forests can be used to make…
quiz.explain: Bamboo is strong and bendy, so it is woven into baskets, mats and even houses.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the uses of bamboo

teach.ask: Gappu wonders why people care so much about forests. What do forests give us?
teach.praise: Wonderful! Forests give us honey, wood and fruits, give animals a home and keep soil and air healthy.
teach.nudge: Name some things we get from forests, and how forests help animals.

learn.hook: Would you hug a tree to protect it? Some brave people did just that!
points: The Bishnoi community of Rajasthan follows rules that say green trees must not be cut and animals must be protected.
In 1730, Amrita Devi Bishnoi of Khejarli village in Rajasthan hugged khejri trees to stop them from being cut. Many villagers joined her.
Bishnois also protect animals like the blackbuck and the chinkara.
In the 1970s, villagers in the hills of Uttarakhand, many of them women, hugged trees to stop them from being cut. This was called the Chipko movement.
'Chipko' means 'to stick' or 'to hug'. Gaura Devi led the women of Reni village in this movement in 1974.

example.q: Think it through: Why did the villagers in the Chipko movement hug the trees?
steps: Workers had come to cut down the trees.
The trees gave the villagers firewood and fodder, and held the soil on the slopes.
By hugging the trees, the villagers stood between the workers and the trees.
example.answer: To stop the trees from being cut, because the forest was important for their lives.

learn.reallife: You can be a nature protector too: save paper, water your school plants and never harm birds or animals.

games.title: Match the nature protectors
pairs: Led the women of Reni village

items.text: The Bishnoi community lives mainly in ___.
The Chipko movement started in the hills of ___.

quiz.q: What did people do in the Chipko movement?
options: They hugged trees to stop them from being cut
quiz.explain: In the Chipko movement, villagers held on to trees so that the trees could not be cut.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what the Chipko movement was

quiz.q: The Chipko movement took place in the hills of which present-day state?
quiz.explain: The Chipko movement happened in the hills that are now in Uttarakhand.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the places of nature movements

quiz.q: Amrita Devi Bishnoi protected khejri trees in which year?
quiz.explain: In 1730, Amrita Devi and the villagers of Khejarli hugged khejri trees to protect them.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the year of the Bishnoi story with the Chipko movement

quiz.q: Which animals are the Bishnoi people famous for protecting?
quiz.explain: Bishnois care for the blackbuck and the chinkara, which roam near their villages in Rajasthan.
quiz.mistake: Picks animals that do not live in Rajasthan

quiz.q: What does the word 'Chipko' mean?
quiz.explain: Chipko means to stick or hug. People hugged the trees.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of Chipko

quiz.q: Gaura Devi is remembered for…
options: leading the women of Reni village to protect trees
quiz.explain: In 1974, Gaura Devi led the women of Reni village in the Chipko movement.
quiz.mistake: Does not know Gaura Devi's role

quiz.q: The Bishnoi community follows a rule about trees. What is it?
quiz.explain: One of the Bishnoi rules is not to cut green, living trees.
quiz.mistake: Does not know Bishnoi beliefs about nature

quiz.q: Why were the trees important to the villagers of the Chipko movement?
options: They were in the way of games
They gave firewood, fodder and held the soil
quiz.explain: The forest gave the villagers firewood and fodder for their animals, and kept the soil safe.
quiz.mistake: Does not see how forests help daily life

teach.ask: Gappu heard that people once hugged trees! Who were they, and why did they do it?
teach.praise: Amazing! The Bishnois and the Chipko villagers hugged trees to stop them from being cut. True heroes of nature!
teach.nudge: What did the villagers do to the trees, and why?

learn.hook: One man planted a whole forest by himself! You can start with one seed.
points: Some communities keep patches of forest as sacred groves. No one cuts trees there, so plants and animals stay safe.
Sacred groves are found in many states, like the kavu of Kerala, the devrai of Maharashtra and the forest of Mawphlang in Meghalaya.
Jadav Payeng of Assam planted trees on a sandy island in the Brahmaputra for many years. It grew into a big forest called the Molai forest.
Saalumarada Thimmakka of Karnataka planted and cared for hundreds of banyan trees along a road.
Van Mahotsav is a tree-planting festival held in the first week of July. World Environment Day is on 5 June.

example.q: Think it through: Why do people plant trees in the first week of July for Van Mahotsav?
steps: In July, the monsoon rains have begun in most of India.
Young plants need lots of water to grow roots.
example.answer: Because the rainy season gives young saplings plenty of water to grow.

learn.reallife: Plant a sapling with your family, give it a name and water it every week. Watch it grow along with you!

games.title: Match the green hero
pairs: Grew the Molai forest in Assam
Planted banyan trees along a road in Karnataka
Forest patch where trees are not cut

games.title: True or false?
items: World Environment Day is on 5 June.
Every year on 5 June, people around the world think about caring for nature.
In a sacred grove, people cut trees freely.
In sacred groves, trees are protected and not cut.
Van Mahotsav is held in the first week of July.
It comes during the rainy season, which helps young trees grow.
A young sapling does not need water.
Saplings need water regularly to grow strong roots.
Jadav Payeng grew a forest in Assam.
He planted trees for many years, and the Molai forest grew.

quiz.q: What is a sacred grove?
options: A patch of forest that a community protects
quiz.explain: Sacred groves are forest patches that communities protect. Trees there are not cut.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what a sacred grove is

quiz.q: Who grew the Molai forest in Assam?
quiz.explain: Jadav Payeng planted trees on a sandy island of the Brahmaputra for years, and the Molai forest grew.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the green heroes

quiz.q: When is World Environment Day celebrated?
quiz.explain: World Environment Day is celebrated every year on 5 June.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up World Environment Day with national holidays

quiz.q: Van Mahotsav is a festival of…
quiz.explain: During Van Mahotsav, people plant saplings all over India.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what Van Mahotsav is

quiz.q: Saalumarada Thimmakka is famous for…
options: planting and caring for banyan trees along a road
quiz.explain: Saalumarada Thimmakka of Karnataka planted hundreds of banyan trees and cared for them like children.
quiz.mistake: Does not know Thimmakka's work

quiz.q: In which month is Van Mahotsav held?
quiz.explain: Van Mahotsav is held in the first week of July, during the rains.
quiz.mistake: Does not link tree-planting with the rainy season

quiz.q: Why are plants and animals safe in a sacred grove?
options: Because it is in the sea
Because it has a fence of steel
Because people do not cut trees or harm living things there
quiz.explain: The community protects the grove, so trees and the animals living there are left in peace.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only fences protect forests

quiz.q: Which is the best way for a child to care for nature?
options: Planting a sapling and watering it
quiz.explain: Planting and caring for a sapling helps nature grow.
quiz.mistake: Does not link everyday actions with caring for nature

teach.ask: Gappu wants more trees for his friends. How do people care for nature today?
teach.praise: Superb! People plant saplings, protect sacred groves and care for trees. Gappu will plant a tree today!
teach.nudge: What can people do to grow and protect forests?
